title: Post-Quantum Security for Original Minalpher
summary: The paper proves post-quantum security only for a fixed-zero-padding Minalpher variant; extending the proof to the original flag- and nonce-dependent construction remains open.

formal_statement.body: Establish post-quantum security for the original Minalpher construction using the tweakable block cipher $MA$, whose key expansion maps $k$ to $(k\mathbin\|\mathsf{flag}\mathbin\|N)\oplus P(k\mathbin\|\mathsf{flag}\mathbin\|N)$, so the flag and nonce $N$, both components of the tweak, affect the tweaked keys. Existing tweakable Even--Mansour analysis based on fixed-zero key padding does not directly cover $MA$. The unresolved task is to prove post-quantum security without replacing this expansion by $k\mapsto(k\mathbin\|0^{n/2})\oplus P(k\mathbin\|0^{n/2})$, or to extend the analysis to handle the original flag- and nonce-dependent key expansion.

scope.domain: Post-quantum security analysis of tweakable Even–Mansour block ciphers and the Minalpher authenticated-encryption construction.
assumptions: P is modeled as a public random permutation.
The post-quantum model permits quantum access to P and only classical access to the secretly keyed construction.
parameters: k: secret-key input to the key-expansion map
N: nonce that is also a tweak component and affects the tweaked keys
flag: tweak component that affects the tweaked keys
n: block-length parameter governing the fixed-zero-padding alternative
P: public permutation used by the key expansion and MA
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove post-quantum security for original Minalpher and MA with flag- and nonce-dependent key expansion, or extend the analysis to cover it without substituting fixed-zero padding.

citations.label: Post-Quantum security of Tweakable Even-Mansour, and Applications

progress.summary: The source explains that fixed-zero-padding analysis does not directly apply when the flag and nonce affect MA's tweaked keys. It establishes post-quantum security for a modified Minalpher0 variant instead, leaving the original construction unresolved.
citation_labels: Gorjan Alagic et al., Post-Quantum security of Tweakable Even-Mansour, and Applications
